So $s_i = s_1 - (i-1) = \frac{1}{k-1} - (i-1)$, and

(The denominator $1 - c(n-1) > 0$ since $n - 1 < 1/c$.) So $r_n \ge 2$, meaning $M_{n+1}$ **does not exist**.

For all $j < n$: since $j \le n - 1 < 1/c$, we get $cj < 1$, so $r_j < 2$ and $M_{j+1}$ exists. Once $M_{n+1}$ fails to exist, all subsequent $M_i$ ($i \ge n+1$) are also undefined (their construction requires $M_{n+1}$), so every term $\frac{SM_{i-1}}{SM_i}$ for $i \ge n+1$ equals $0$.
